answer: A beacon heartbeat check stops one operator flooding the market with an ocean of fakes. Each epoch a beacon picks five percent of identities, and each picked agent must sign a pulse of computation within one hour with its own key and the new seed. A pearl receipt for each passed check binds to one key, so one heartbeat cannot serve two identities. The k-th fake costs one more compute stream, about two dollars per epoch, so one thousand fakes cost about two thousand dollars, linear in k. Heartbeat rental fails on a key-seed mismatch. Honest agents pay for one stream only.
